paragraphs: Rav Acha bar Uya is mentioned in [Pesachim 33b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.33b.2). Hyman says that [Seder HaDorot](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=261&lang=en) conflates Avya and Uya, whom he considers unrelated.

notes.text: The frozen acronym is סה״ר and is not expanded here. The source explicitly rejects conflating אויא and עויא; no identity merge is made.

In [Heilprin’s Avya entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=261&lang=en), Rav Acha bar Avya appears under Avya, and Heilprin asks whether Avya and Avya the Elder were one person or two.

Hyman’s printed page (vol. III, p. 970) has סה״ד, where the supplied Hebrew has סה״ר. The linked Bavli’s Hebrew gives Rav Acha bar Rav Uya (עויא), while its English gives Avya. [Heilprin’s list of Rabbi Yochanan’s transmitters](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=1828&lang=en) includes both Rav Acha bar Avira and Rav Acha bar Uya. Hyman objects to conflating Avya and Uya.
